content.title: Rand Paul presses Mullin on past assault remarks
content.text: Skip to contentHomeNewsSportBusinessTechnologyHealthCultureArtsTravelEarthAudioVideoLiveDocumentariesWeatherNewslettersWatch Live0:55Rand Paul presses Mullin on past assault remarksKentucky Senator Rand Paul, who leads the Senate Committee on Homeland Security, spoke about political violence in his opening remarks, including an attack Paul himself faced where he had six of his ribs broken by a neighbour in 2017.Paul questioned if someone who applauds political violence is the right person to lead the Department of Homeland Security, while offering President Donald Trump's pick to become the new leader of the Department of Homeland Security, Senator MarkWayne Mullin, the chance to apologise for reportedly previously saying he understood why a neighbour attacked Paul, a Republican.18 March 2026United StatesShareSaveExplore MorePlane and firetruck removed from runway after LaGuardia crashFirst Lady Melania Trump arrives with humanoid robot at tech summitDog rescued after falling into a 12-foot (3.6m) sinkholeWhat happened in the seconds before Air Canada plane crashed at LaGuardia'Helpful' and 'scary': Travellers react to ICE agents at airportsExplosion at Texas oil refinery creates huge smoke plumeHow the deadly LaGuardia Airport crash unfolded'Stop, stop, stop': Listen to LaGuardia control tower audio during collisionBBC in Cuba as island plunged into darknessBBC asks Chuck Norris about being a 'successful, really terrible' actorRecord-breaking heatwave hits the US WestRos Atkins on...
